summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of T2 paraplegia, restrictive ventilatory defect on home oxygen, and recurrent infections was admitted with dyspnea and cough. She was found to have septic shock and Stenotrophomonas bacteremia likely originating from her tunneled central line. Imaging revealed new left lower lobe opacities consistent with pneumonia, and sputum culture grew MRSA. She was treated with vancomycin and cefepime initially, then transitioned to Bactrim after blood cultures confirmed Stenotrophomonas. The central line was removed, and she completed a course of IV antibiotics. She also experienced transient toxic encephalopathy and withdrawal symptoms related to polysubstance use, which resolved. Her anemia was managed with a blood transfusion, and heart failure symptoms improved with diuresis. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics with follow-up arranged in multiple specialties.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
